records.kind: state oversight body's formal correction of a central bank subsidiary
records.summary: The Control Yuan, Taiwan's constitutional oversight branch, formally corrected the Central Mint (中央造幣廠), a subsidiary of the Central Bank of the Republic of China, for failing to investigate a workplace-bullying complaint by a former deputy director in the manner required by the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Ministry of Labour's Guidelines on Preventing Unlawful Infringement in the Performance of Duties as revised on 18 August 2022 (ROC 111). The correction text records that the Mint's handling 'was clearly negligent' and transmits the case to the Central Bank to require its subordinate Mint to review and improve. The correction is made under Article 97(1) of the Constitution and Article 24 of the Control Act. DATE NOTE: the correction text at source_url carries no date on its face; the Control Yuan's own file for it sits in the ROC year 114 (2025) series and the .docx file's internal creation timestamp is 2025-03-20, so the month is taken from the document file itself and is stated here as derived, not as a date printed on the page. SECOND SOURCE for the case number and closure: the Control Yuan Finance and Economics Committee's correction-case closing table at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/72060 identifies the case as 114財正0002 against the Central Mint, records the Central Bank's reply that the Mint revised its prevention plan in May 2025 (ROC 114 年 5 月) and that the Mint's handling of the complaint '容有加強空間', and records the committee closing the case on 114.06.04, i.e. 4 June 2025.
records.detail: This is the state acting on the central bank's own works rather than the bank acting as regulator: the Control Yuan is an organ of the state, the Central Mint is a central bank subsidiary, and the correction instrument was addressed through the Central Bank of the Republic of China with a duty to report back on remedial action. It is not a corruption finding, which is why it is filed on the removals-and-pressure row rather than the case row. The complainant and the officials named inside the correction appear only as initials or redacted surnames (A君, 葉〇〇), so no individual is named here.
records.quote: 中央造幣廠的處理，顯有怠失，應予糾正促其注意改善。
records.source_title: 監察院 糾正案文 — 被糾正機關：中央造幣廠 (114財正2 公告)

records.kind: parliamentary committee recommends the governor's removal
records.summary: The People's Majlis Public Accounts (public finance) Committee approved a motion, moved by Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim, recommending that President Mohamed Muizzu remove Ali Hashim from the post of Governor of the Maldives Monetary Authority, on the ground that the committee found he had not been performing the governor's duties effectively while the government was raising funds on the domestic market, and that the MMA had given the government no advice on the objectives set out in the MMA Act since 17 November 2023. Hashim, who was ill, answered the committee in writing instead of attending and replied that the government had disregarded the central bank's advice, which he said had produced the country's economic difficulties. The motion was to go to the full Majlis before being put to the President. DATE NOTE: the VFP report at source_url is dated 17 July 2024 and says the committee approved the motion 'on Wednesday', which is that same date; the day is therefore taken from the report's publication date and is stated here as derived rather than as a date printed in the body of the page. The report also states the motion was submitted to parliament on 2 July. SECOND SOURCE: the state broadcaster PSM News at https://www.psmnews.mv/en/140589 carries the same committee decision, records that it passed by a majority of the members attending, that Hashim declined three invitations to appear and sent a written report, that the committee found the MMA had not advised the government since 17 November 2023, and that a proposal to give him one further chance to reply in writing was voted down.
records.detail: This is a second and distinct episode from the one the map already holds for the Maldives, which is the Majlis suspending the fiscal responsibility law in November 2021 to let the government overdraw the central bank. Here the organ of the state is the Majlis committee and the object is the governor's tenure, with different actors, a different year and a different instrument. Both the VFP report and the PSM News report are press rather than the Majlis's own minutes, so this rests on news reporting of a committee decision; the Majlis's own committee pages for the 20th Parliament's Public Accounts Committee exist at majlis.gov.mv but were not opened within this round's fetch budget. SOURCE CONFLICT ON THE VOTE: the two reports do not agree on how the committee carried the motion. VFP says the committee unanimously supported the recommendation; PSM News says it passed by a majority of the members who attended. Neither figure is reconcilable with the other and the Majlis's own minutes were not read, so this record states the motion was approved and does not state the margin. VFP also puts the gap in the governor's advice at 'the past seven months' where PSM gives a start date of 17 November 2023, which is eight months before the committee met; the date here is PSM's, read by hand on 17 November 2026 because psmnews.mv answers 403 to scripted fetches and opens for a browser.
records.source_title: VFP — Finance Committee Recommends Removal of Central Bank Governor

blanks.note: ECB Opinion CON/2023/39 of 6 December 2023, read in full from the mirror at https://www.naftemporiki.gr/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/ecb.pdf (8 pages, sections 1.1-1.3 and the whole assessment). It is an opinion requested by the Greek Ministry of Finance on draft tax amendments excluding cash purchases of real estate and lowering the cash-deduction threshold from EUR 500 to EUR 300. It says nothing about the Bank of Greece's independence, functions or finances, so it is not an act against the national central bank and was refused rather than filed. Greece's single existing record is the May 2015 government-versus-Stournaras episode, which this does not touch.

ECB Opinion CON/2018/23 was located and identified but its text was never opened. The EUR-Lex record at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52018AB0023 gives the full title and date - 'Opinion of the European Central Bank of 11 May 2018 on the governance and financial independence of the Central Bank of Cyprus (CON/2018/23)' - but EUR-Lex serves no text body for it (the /TXT/HTML/ variant answers 'The requested document does not exist'), and the record carries no link to an ECB PDF. Four constructed ecb.europa.eu/ecb/legal/pdf/ filenames for it (en_con_2018_23_f_sign.pdf, en_con_2018_23.pdf, con_2018_23_f_sign.pdf, celex_52018ab0023_en_txt.pdf) all returned 404. A title alone does not state that the draft law damaged the bank, so nothing was filed. Cyprus is the single best remaining lead on this row: the opinion's own title names the Central Bank of Cyprus's governance AND financial independence, and Cyprus's one existing record is the March 2014 Demetriades resignation, four years earlier. CON/2013/41, CON/2013/54, CON/2013/78, CON/2013/10 and CON/2019/24 all surfaced alongside it and are unopened.

Searched the Maltese Parliament's own site for a second episode. parlament.mt carries 'Motion no 322 - Central Bank' (13th legislature) and the Speaker's ruling 'SO 13 - lack of resignation or dismissal of the Governor CBM and the PS in the MEEP' (14th legislature), and press records a PN request on 13 May 2024 for an urgent debate on Edward Scicluna that the Speaker refused. Every one of these is the same 2024 Scicluna episode the map already holds as the 30 July 2024 suspension, so filing any of them would re-file that episode under a different description. No earlier Maltese episode surfaced. ECB Opinion CON/2006/23 on a Central Bank of Malta Act amendment exists and its draft-law annex is at ecb.europa.eu/ecb/legal/pdf/con_2006_23_draft_law.pdf, unopened.

Searched for Eesti Pank's or the ECB's written objections to draft Estonian legislation. Every ECB opinion that surfaced (CON/2020/02, CON/2020/07, CON/2014/21, CON/2008/14) came back only as lagen.nu mirror pages, which are robots-disallowed and were not fetched, and no Eesti Pank-hosted opinion or formal objection was found. Nothing on eestipank.ee was opened, so Estonia has not actually been tested on this vein.

Same result as Estonia. ECB opinions on Lithuanian draft law surfaced only as lagen.nu mirrors (CON/2005/38, CON/2009/26, CON/2012/63, CON/2013/45, CON/2025/23) plus a law-firm summary of an opinion on Lithuania's CRD VI transposition at finreg.aoshearman.com. No Lietuvos bankas page and no opinion text was opened.

Not a research blank but a data note the next round should act on. have_events.json already holds two Kyrgyz records filed with kind 'other', which the brief says the map counts nowhere: index 82, 26 June 2024, the Jogorku Kenesh relieving the head of the National Bank of his post (24.kg/english/297673), and index 92, 18 March 2026, the National Bank head submitting a letter of resignation (24.kg/english/366517). The first of these is on its face a parliament removing a governor, i.e. exactly this row. Re-kinding an existing record is not a new record and was not filed here, but if index 82 were given a real kind Kyrgyzstan would move off 'exactly one' with no fetches at all.

Recorded for completeness: the one concrete unopened lead named in the assignment, Control Yuan correction 114財正0002, was opened and filed. The correction text serves to plain curl at multimedia.cy.gov.tw with the backslash-separated path exactly as the search returned it, and the Finance and Economics Committee's closing tables serve at cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/<id>. Two neighbouring tables were read: id 72060 covers 114財正0002 (the Central Mint bullying case) and id 71673 covers investigation report 114財調0009, which records the Central Bank being made to supervise the Mint's revision of its staff-grievance committee rules and the Mint concluding a draft collective agreement with its union on 7 February 2025 - a further unworked Taiwanese lead on the same subsidiary. id 73824 is 114財正0003 and concerns solar power, not the bank.

A sourcing finding worth more than one record, since the assignment names ECB Opinions as this row's best unworked vein. ecb.europa.eu now answers plain curl on /ecb/legal/pdf/ with a JavaScript interstitial on paths that exist (en_con_2016_52_en.pdf returned 200 and 113,908 bytes of HTML, not a PDF) and a 97KB HTML 404 page on paths that do not, so the route named in the brief no longer works as described and a 200 there must be checked for content type. BUT: eur-lex.europa.eu answers plain curl fully, its quick search works, and CON/YYYY/NN maps mechanically to CELEX 5YYYYABNNNN - a search for the string "CON/2018/23" returned CELEX 52018AB0023 as its first hit. /legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:5YYYYABNNNN then gives the opinion's exact official title and adoption date, which for opinions on central bank law usually names the bank and the subject of the complaint. What it does NOT give is the body text, so EUR-Lex alone can identify and date candidates across every EU member in this list at near-zero cost but cannot by itself support a record. Pairing EUR-Lex identification with a national central bank or national gazette copy of the text is the method the next round should use.
